title: egress-probe-policy-false-positive-investigation-2026-03-13
body:
Summary:
During a scheduled synthetic egress check on 2026-03-11 07:42 UTC, our control plane alerted that ~12% of customer-private clusters were returning transient "blocked" status for outbound probes to our telemetry endpoint. Alerts aggregated at 07:45 UTC and automatically triggered an on-call SRE paging rule. Initial impact: customers using Private/VPC mode saw control-plane health checks report "egress unavailable" (false negative) which caused our rollouts to fall back to diagnostic mode for affected tenants. No customer traffic was actually dropped — only our synthetic probes were affected.

Why this is interesting/different:
Most past egress failures have been caused by obvious ACLs, NAT exhaustion, or path MTU problems. This incident turned out to be a false positive generated by a mismatch between our probe packet characteristics and some customer-managed firewall DPI heuristics combined with an overly-broad egress policy on a middlebox appliance. The combination produced a short window where probes were inspected and reset, while actual customer application connections (TLS to 443) were allowed.

Timeline (all times UTC):
- 2026-03-11 07:42:03: Synthetic probe runner (controlplane/prober-v2) sent 60s batch of UDP-based probes to telemetry.redwood.example:53001 from ephemeral port range.
- 07:42:07: Probe failures started surfacing in probe logs (5% error rate).
- 07:45:12: Alerting threshold crossed (>=10% failure) and on-call paged (SRE rotation).
- 07:48:30: Pager acknowledged; initial triage attempted connecting to affected cluster controlplane via SSH into bastion — normal.
- 07:55:00: Packet captures requested on customer gateway VM and on our prober instance.
- 08:05:18: tcpdump on gateway shows RSTs/ICMP-unreach generated by firewall appliance after inspecting packet payload.
- 08:12:40: Confirmed that customer had an appliance (Acme DPI v3.2) with an egress signature configured to block 'unexpected UDP flows to high-range ports' for a subset of subnets.
- 08:30:00: Temporary mitigation implemented: prober switched to TCP/TLS-based probes on port 443 and resumed successful checks.
- 09:05:00: Outreach started to customer network ops with packet captures and hypothesis.
- 11:20:00: Customer confirmed appliance logs showing DPI signature matched and dropped probe flows; they applied exception for prober IP range.
- 13:45:00: Control plane health returned to normal; alert resolved.

Root cause (short):
1) Our synthetic prober uses UDP probes (low-overhead) that mimic some telemetry collectors.
2) A subset of customers run a DPI appliance configured with an aggressive signature that treats short UDP flows to ephemeral/high ports as suspicious and issues resets or ICMP unreachable messages.
3) The appliance's egress policy was broad and applied to multiple internal subnets; it had no exception for our known prober IP ranges.
4) Our health-checking logic treated probe failures as equivalent to customer egress failures, leading to false degradation signals and automated rollbacks/diagnostic modes.

Contributing factors:
- Prober protocol choice: UDP probes are cheap but less likely to survive middlebox inspection.
- Rule placement: customer had appliance in-line at the egress without explicit allowlist for controlplane probes.
- Observability gap: probe traces didn't include packet metadata (DF flag, payload signature) by default, delaying root-cause identification.
- Alert sensitivity: thresholds didn't differentiate probe-protocol classes.

Immediate mitigation applied:
- Switched synthetic probes to a TCP/TLS fallback on port 443 for the affected regions (automated in prober config) — reduces false positives for midbox inspection.
- Opened a comms channel with affected customers; provided packet captures and recommended exceptions.
- Temporarily suppressed rollout automation that used probe-only health to trigger aborts for the impacted customer segments.

Longer-term remediation plan (proposed):
1) Prober hardening (owner: Marco Alvarez, due: 2026-04-02):
   - Make probe protocol and port configurable per-customer, default to TCP/TLS over 443 for Private clusters.
   - Add a prober mode that sends an initial TCP/TLS handshake before any UDP sampling.
   - Improve probe metadata: record DF/MSS/TTL and full 5-tuple in probe traces.

2) Health evaluation refinement (owner: Priya Patel, due: 2026-04-09):
   - Add protocol-aware thresholds (separate UDP probe metrics from TCP/TLS probe metrics) to prevent UDP probe noise from failing health checks.
   - Add a secondary check that attempts a customer-traffic-similar TCP/TLS flow before triggering rollout abort.

3) Customer onboarding checklist update (owner: Jordan Lee, due: 2026-04-16):
   - Update the Private/VPC onboarding guide to recommend inserting allowlist entries for our prober IPs and specify recommended DPI exceptions.
   - Provide sample firewall rules for common appliances (Acme DPI, BigFence, CloudGate).

4) Observability improvements (owner: SRE-observability, due: 2026-05-01):
   - Surface midbox close events (ICMP-unreach, TCP-RST seen by prober) as first-class signals in the Console.
   - Add dashboards showing probe protocol split and failure attribution by reason.

Post-incident runbook draft (quick ops steps) - to be added to oncall playbooks:
1) When prober failures observed >= 8% for > 5min in private clusters:
   - Step 1: Run prober status command on controlplane host: /usr/local/bin/proberctl status --region <region> --since 10m
   - Step 2: Check recent probe logs for protocol and dest-port: /var/log/prober/prober.log | grep "probe-failed" | tail -n 100
   - Step 3: If failures are UDP-only, switch prober to TLS-443 fallback: /usr/local/bin/proberctl set-protocol --mode fallback-tcp --commit; wait 60s and re-run status
   - Step 4: Collect packet capture on the customer's gateway VM (if accessible): sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host <probe-ip> and port <dest-port> -w /tmp/probe.pcap (collect 30s)
   - Step 5: If tcpdump shows ICMP-unreach or firewall-inserted RSTs, contact customer NET-ops and request DPI signature ID and exception for probe-ip-range.
   - Step 6: Temporarily disable automated rollouts for the customer (console -> deployments -> <customer> -> pause automated health aborts).

Commands & quick checklist for triage:
- proberctl tail /var/log/prober/prober.log --lines 200
- sudo tcpdump -n -i any host <probe-ip> and port <dest-port> -c 500 -w /tmp/probe.pcap
- sudo conntrack -L | grep <probe-ip>
- sudo nft list ruleset | sed -n '1,200p'  # inspect firewall config on VM-level
- journalctl -u prober -S "2026-03-11" | grep -i error

Customer coordination template (email/Slack):
Subject: "Redwood control-plane probes impacted by DPI signature - packet captures attached"
Hi <NET-ops>,
We observed your appliance (model X) dropping short UDP flows matching a signature used to block suspicious traffic. Our probes are lightweight UDP packets that your DPI treats as threats. We can switch to TCP/TLS-based probes or you can add a temporary allowlist for the following prober IP ranges: 203.0.113.128/28, 198.51.100.64/28.
Attached: packet capture + timestamped logs. Please share the appliance signature ID and we will coordinate a safe exception window.

Lessons learned and notes:
- Defaulting to UDP probes for Private clusters is fragile across heterogeneous customer middleboxes.
- We need to treat synthetic probes as a customer-facing artifact; document recommended firewall exceptions during onboarding.
- Better signal correlation (ICMP/TCP events) would have reduced time-to-detect root cause by ~30 minutes.

Open action items (summary):
- Marco: prober config change to prefer TCP/TLS by default for Private clusters (due 2026-04-02)
- Priya: health-eval changes in control-plane to add protocol-aware thresholds (due 2026-04-09)
- Jordan: update onboarding docs and add sample firewall rules (due 2026-04-16)
- SRE-observability: surface midbox-close signals in Console (due 2026-05-01)
- Ops: add runbook excerpt to oncall playbook and train this rotation (owner: oncall-lead, due 2026-03-27)

Appendix: artifacts collected during investigation:
- prober logs: /var/lib/redwood/archives/prober-2026-03-11-07.tgz
- packet captures (redacted): /mnt/incident/pcaps/probe-priv-gw-20260311.pcap
- appliance logs (shared by customer): acme-dpi-log-2026-03-11-07.txt

Notes for reviewers:
This is intentionally written as an ops-facing investigation + runbook draft. The primary goal is to reduce false-positive egress alerts driven by synthetic probes and avoid unnecessary automated rollbacks. Feedback requested on: protocol fallback behavior, recommended default probe for new Private tenants, and wording for onboarding firewall rules.

End of document."
